messages.author: 269e905d87d26565
messages.subject: Scantwo results interpretation
parts:
Dear All,

I ran both scanone and scantwo analaysis to explore and identify the QTLs linked to my trait. Using the scanone I got three QTL on chr 3, 4 and 5. Then, I tried the CIM analysis to see if I could find other QTLs while controling for the ones that were already identified and no further QTL was found. However, I was a bit troubled after running a scantwo analysis and now I am not sure If I am interpreting that well.

Here the results of the scantwo :

> summary(out17,perms=operm17,alphas=c(0.05,0.05,0,0.05,0.05),pvalues=TRUE)
 pos1f pos2f lod.full pval lod.fv1 pval lod.int pval
c3:c4 20.2 40.4 9.30 0 4.63 0.020 0.5676 1
c3:c5 20.2 10.0 10.02 0 4.76 0.015 0.1099 1
c4:c5 14.2 10.0 8.82 0 3.56 0.135 0.0124 1
pos1a pos2a lod.add pval lod.av1 pval
c3:c4 20.2 25.6 8.73 0 4.07 0.000
c3:c5 20.2 10.0 9.91 0 4.65 0.000
c4:c5 14.2 10.0 8.81 0 3.55 0.002   

So here is what I understand from the R/qtl guide, I would like to make sure that understood well so tell me if I am wrong :

The locations for the QTLs on chr 3 and 5 are the same no matter if we consider the pos of the full model posf or of the additive model posa, is that right ?
But with the lines in green it seems that there are two QTLs on chr 4 that are not located at the same place right ? One is at 40.4 cM for posf / 25.6 cM for posa (first line) and the other one is at 14.2cM for both posf and posa. So the fact that I have two lines with chr 4 with different locations means that I might have two QTLs there ? With only additive effect as the lod.int is very small ?

Compared to scanone and using CIM, both QTLs on 3 and 5 were found at the same location but the QTL on chr 4 identified with scanone was located at 14.2cM when B3 was used as covariate and 25.6cM with B3 and B5 as covariates.

The shape of the courbe could suggest the existence of QTLs on the location 14, 25 and 40cM as we can see high peaks at these locations for the SIM that is why I ran the scantwo to see which QTLs were really detected.

Thank you all for your help !

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Scantwo results interpretation
parts:
With no evidence for interactions, I'd focus on the estimated positions with additive QTL.
chr 3 at 20.2, chr 5 at 10.0, and chr 4 at 14.2-25.6.

The locus on chr 4 moves to position 40.4 when you include an interaction with the chr 3 QTL, but since there's no evidence for an interaction, I would just ignore that.

I'd use makeqtl(), fitqtl(), and refineqtl(), to bring the three QTL together into a single model. You can use addqtl() to scan for an additional QTL, for example to see whether there is evidence for an additional QTL on chr 4.

karl

parts:
Thank you Karl !

 

Indeed, while waiting for your answer I tried to fit a 3 QTL model with fitqtl : B3 + B4 +B5. I tried fitting it with B4 at 14.2 with B3 and B5  = model 1 and also with B4 at 25.6 with B3 and B5 = model 2. When I do that both models seemed to support the data right ? But then when I try to fit a model with 4 QTLs (B3 + B5 and both QTLs on B4), I obtain the results of Model 3. Then, how can I know which one the best fitting model ?

 Model 1

 Model 2

Model 3

 Then, I tried like you asked me to use refineqtl and the position at 14.2 on B4 did change to 25.6. Does that mean that the most likely position is 25.6 cM?

 Finally I tried the addqtl with the refined QTL position (25.6 cM for B4) and got this :

> max(out.aqa17) chr pos lod

MarkerY B3 25.6 1.06

The LOD being so small I don't think that it is a real QTL. Am I right ?

 

Then out of curiosity, I tried with the QTL at 14.2 on B4 in the QTL formula and got this :

> max(out.aqa17) chr pos lod

MarkerX B4 64.7 1.21

Same thing here, there is no evidence for an additional QTL right ?

 

Then, what was observed in the two-QTL scan wasn't right ? Or how can I explain this ?

messages.subject: Re: Scantwo results interpretation
parts:
Confidence intervals for QTL location can be very wide; for weaker QTL, it’s not unusual to have the interval cover nearly the whole chromosome.

Regarding your second question, it is hard to answer without more details. The significance thresholds in scantwo are different from the penalties used in stepwiseqtl.

karl

With no evidence for interactions, I'd focus on the estimated positions with additive QTL.
chr 3 at 20.2, chr 5 at 10.0, and chr 4 at 14.2-25.6.

karl
